english.title: Use on a road a trailer the maximum permitted laden weight exceeded
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), used on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), a trailer, the maximum permitted laden weight of 44,000 kg was exceeded by **(..SPECIFY THE EXCESS WEIGHT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 75(3) of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986, section 41B of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
used on a road a trailer the laden weight of which
exceeded the maximum permitted laden weight

english.notes:
(i) See column 2 of the table to regulation 75 for applicable classes of vehicle and column 3 for the relevant maximum permitted laden weight.
(ii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant used a trailer, on **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..).

The maximum permitted laden weight for the trailer was 44,000 kgs. It exceeded such weight by **(..SPECIFY THE EXCESS WEIGHT..) kg.

This represented an overload of **(..SPECIFY..) %.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Fixed penalty ticket - One hundred pounds.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
